card: Optimizes BIP352 silent payment input eligibility checks by filtering out non-segwit P2SH inputs before evaluating their scriptSig. For non-segwit P2SH spends, this avoids parsing and evaluating scripts up to MAX_SCRIPT_SIZE by verifying witness requirements first. If implemented incorrectly, silent payment scanning could misclassify eligible inputs and miss incoming transactions.
evidence: PR description: 'Consensus forbids a witness on non-segwit P2SH inputs, so check the witness (and the cheap pubkey size check) before evaluating the scriptSig. This avoids evaluating scriptSigs of up to MAX_SCRIPT_SIZE for the common case of non-segwit P2SH spends.'
problem: When scanning inputs for BIP352 eligibility, verifying whether a P2SH input is P2SH-P2WPKH currently evaluates the scriptSig even for non-segwit P2SH spends. Because scriptSigs can be up to 10,000 bytes, running script evaluation on ordinary non-segwit P2SH inputs incurs unnecessary CPU overhead during block or transaction scanning.

risk.why: A flaw in silent payment input eligibility checking could cause nodes or wallets to skip eligible inputs or compute incorrect tweaks, leading to missed transactions.

scope_notes: Small 10-line optimization in BIP352 input handling logic.
summary: Optimizes BIP352 silent payment input eligibility verification for P2SH inputs. It checks for a non-empty witness and valid public key size before evaluating the input scriptSig, allowing non-segwit P2SH spends to be skipped without evaluating scripts up to MAX_SCRIPT_SIZE.
